findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted/dead feature-flag logic and always returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is actually true when the flag is *disabled*), and then returns `false` in both branches. The feature-flag lookup is therefore meaningless and the variable name is misleading. While the net effect (SQL expressions always rejected) is the intended security outcome, this reads like a half-finished gate: a future maintainer trying to 're-enable behind the flag' by changing the first `return false` to `return true` would actually enable SQL expressions when the flag is OFF. If the intent is an unconditional kill-switch, drop the flag check and return false directly (or a constant) with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264; if the intent is flag-gated, fix the negation.

findings.title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This is a fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), but the PR adds no test that (a) `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled, (b) `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` fail for any non-empty SQL, and (c) `sql.DB.QueryFramesInto`/`RunCommands`/`TablesList` return errors. Without such tests, a later refactor (e.g. someone 'fixing' the odd logic in `enableSqlExpressions`, or re-adding a real DB implementation behind `NewInMemoryDB`) could silently re-expose the vulnerable path. Add unit tests in `pkg/expr` and `pkg/expr/sql` that lock in the disabled behavior.

findings.title: Every SQL expression attempt now logs a misleading ERROR with the user's raw SQL
findings.body: `TablesList` still escapes the SQL, builds a `json_serialize_sql` command and calls `duckDB.RunCommands`, which now unconditionally returns `not implemented`. The result is that every user attempt to use a SQL expression emits `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ..., "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)` followed by `logger.Warn("invalid sql query", ...)` in `NewSQLCommand`. The message is wrong (nothing is being serialized; the feature is disabled), it is at ERROR level for an expected/handled condition, and it dumps user-supplied SQL into server logs twice per request. Since the function can never succeed, it should short-circuit with a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' error (and the now-dead `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` helpers and the `flatten` import can be removed) rather than exercising the old pipeline.

findings.title: sqlExpressions feature toggle remains documented/exposed but has no effect
findings.body: After this change the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle (`featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions`) is still registered and documented as enabling SQL expressions, but enabling it does nothing: `ReadQuery` returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented` and the `sql.DB` stub errors on every call. Users who follow the existing feature-toggle documentation will enable the flag and get a confusing 'not implemented' error. Either mark the toggle as disabled/removed in its registration and docs, or update the toggle description to state that the feature has been disabled for security reasons.
